module purpose: neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter decodes shift commands from ctrl_i and shifts rs1_i by shamt_i. Depending on the FAST_SHIFT_EN generic it either iterates a serial shifter with internal state or computes the shift through a barrel network, then drives res_o and valid_o.

use-case flows.value: supported shift-command decision from ctrl_i that starts the serial shifter or qualifies the fast path
serial shift execution: load operand and count, decrement the count, and shift the register left or right until done
barrel shift execution: prepare the input orientation and sign fill, apply shamt_i-selected stages, register the result, and drive the output
valid_o reports serial completion when not FAST_SHIFT_EN or accepted-command validity when FAST_SHIFT_EN
serial shifter state and fast-path result buffer cleared while rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes valid_cmd only for the ctrl_i combinations in lines 65-68. That decision starts the serial path by setting busy and loading cnt and sreg (lines 87-95), and in FAST_SHIFT_EN builds it also qualifies the barrel input and is copied to valid_o (lines 122, 144). Integrity requires that only those implemented command encodings are accepted; availability is that the decision is produced whenever the predicate in lines 65-68 holds.

The requested amount is stored into shifter.cnt on a valid command (line 94), decremented during serial execution (line 97), and read back through shifter.run and shifter.done to control continuation and termination (lines 108-109) when FAST_SHIFT_EN is false. When FAST_SHIFT_EN is true, each shamt_i bit selects whether a barrel stage shifts or passes through (lines 128-129). Integrity of this value preserves the implemented shift distance and, in serial mode, the termination point; availability is the retained and decremented count under the conditions of lines 94-109.

The module captures rs1_i into the serial shift register on line 95 and, when not FAST_SHIFT_EN, updates that register by the left-shift or right-shift rules in lines 98-101 until the value is driven to res_o on line 111. When FAST_SHIFT_EN is true, lines 122-123 prepare the barrel-shifter input and sign fill, lines 128-129 apply the shamt_i-selected shifts, line 138 registers bs_result, and line 143 drives the final output. Integrity requires res_o to match these implemented transformations; availability applies when the accepted operation reaches its output condition.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial shift status and completion state
conceptual assets.reasoning: Only when FAST_SHIFT_EN is false, the module keeps execution status in shifter.busy, setting it on a valid command and clearing it on done or ctrl_i.cpu_trap (lines 87-90). Completion is computed from the counter in line 109, latched into shifter.done_ff by line 86, reported on valid_o by line 110, and used to release res_o on line 111. Integrity of this state keeps completion, abort, and result release aligned with the implemented serial protocol; availability applies because the status must progress from start to completion or trap-driven clear.
